claim: Let \(\Gamma=(K_{1,m},\sigma)\) be a signed star with \(m\ge3\) leaves, centre \(c\), \(p=d^+_\sigma(c)\) positive incident edges, and \(q=m-p=d^-_\sigma(c)\) negative incident edges. Then its plurality number is \[ Y(\Gamma)=\begin{cases} m,&p=0,\\ \max\{p+2,q+1\},&1\le p\le m-1,\\ m+1,&p=m. \end{cases} \] Consequently, because every signing of a tree lies in the switching class of the all-positive signing, \[ \min_{\Gamma'\sim K_{1,m}^+}Y(\Gamma')=\left\lceil\frac{m+3}{2}\right\rceil. \] Equivalently, the reachable-colouring code of the all-positive signed star has covering radius \(\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor\).
integrity: The universal statement is proved directly from the spread-before-ignition dynamics. The verifier independently simulates the definition for every signing in the stated finite range. The initiating source is used for definitions, switching facts, and the general code-radius relation; no independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to finite signed stars with at least three leaves. It does not classify arbitrary signed trees or other signed graph families. The finite exhaustive verifier covers stars with three through eight leaves and does not replace the universal proof. Very recent unindexed equivalent work remains a residual originality risk.
title: Exact plurality number of signed stars
